fix_commit_message:
[autofit] Prevent signed integer overflow.

Reported as

    https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/499135336

* src/autofit/aflatin.c (af_move_contour_vertically): Use `ADD_LONG`.
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix ef54557bda3b on top of intro 7099b09e9629 via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (IntegerOverflow): The autofit module's new vertical separation adjustment feature (added to fix overlapping-contour rendering) moves the points of a glyph contour vertically by directly adding a computed `movement` integer to each point's signed `y` coordinate using a plain `+=` operator. For crafted or degenerate font glyph data, the computed movement combined with existing coordinate values can overflow the signed integer type, which is undefined behavior in C and was detected by OSS-Fuzz/UBSan (issue 499135336). Root cause: The new af_move_contour_vertically() function, introduced along with the vertical separation adjustment feature, performs raw signed addition (`point->y += movement;`) without using FreeType's overflow-safe arithmetic helper macros (e.g. `ADD_LONG`), which are used elsewhere in the codebase precisely to avoid undefined behavior from signed integer overflow when combining glyph coordinate values with computed adjustments.
